Specifically, we'll implement a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) framework for document-grounded reasoning, focusing on:\\n\\n- Data Curation,\\n- Preprocessing, and\\n- Inference &amp; Decoding Logic.\",\"content_type\":\"prose\",\"estimated_tokens\":112,\"section_header\":\"Introduction\",\"parent_section\":null,\"top_header\":\"Introduction\",\"prev_chunk_id\":\"9ae0503a-7b1f-4471-a7fd-0dec634147e9\",\"next_chunk_id\":\"6e2c3b41-1acd-479a-a1ba-7120c4115374\",\"quality_score\":100.0,\"should_use\":1},{\"chunk_id\":\"6e2c3b41-1acd-479a-a1ba-7120c4115374\",\"file_id\":\"6d1dc034-2a37-4157-b297-449b5eb29b24\",\"chunk_index\":2,\"content\":\"In this project, we'll implement a RAG framework for reasoning tasks, using pre-trained weights to summarize information retrieved from unstructured web-crawled data and WARC archives.\\n\\n<!-- image -->\\n\\nFigure A. The system workflow (Created by   Kuriko IWAI  )\\n\\nThe workflow begins when a user submits a query and an HTML reference via the Streamlit interface.\\n\\nThe backend, powered by FastAPI , extracts and structures the raw text into a prompt for the model.\\n\\nThen, the system utilizes a custom BPE tokenizer (orange boxes) to process the user query and crawled data, feeding them into a uniquely configured GPT-based model (green box).\\n\\nThe model then performs an autoregressive process to generate a response by predicting subsequent tokens.\\n\\nFinally, the BPE tokenizer decodes these tokens into human-readable text for the user.\",\"content_type\":\"prose\",\"estimated_tokens\":168,\"section_header\":\"The System Architecture\",\"parent_section\":null,\"top_header\":\"The System Architecture\",\"prev_chunk_id\":\"b396cf9b-ebab-4cfa-8fc1-75aa62dfcfe4\",\"next_chunk_id\":\"e0fe3291-662f-4e13-b497-c60c6641f750\",\"quality_score\":100.0,\"should_use\":1},{\"chunk_id\":\"e0fe3291-662f-4e13-b497-c60c6641f750\",\"file_id\":\"6d1dc034-2a37-4157-b297-449b5eb29b24\",\"chunk_index\":3,\"content\":\"Among Common Crawl's three primary file formats shown in Figure A , WET (extracted text) is the most frequently used for LLM training because processing raw WARC/HTML files at scale is an operational burden.\\n\\nWhile WAT provides richer metadata, including HTML tags and link structures, WET is preferred for its pure textual format.\\n\\nAlthough WARC is rarely used for standard LLM training due to its massive storage footprint, it remains invaluable for multimodal datasets.\\n\\nWe'll opt for WARC in this project to implement custom filters and recover high-signal data discarded during the standard WET extraction process.\",\"content_type\":\"prose\",\"estimated_tokens\":123,\"section_header\":\"WARC for High-Signal Extraction\",\"parent_section\":null,\"top_header\":\"WARC for High-Signal Extraction\",\"prev_chunk_id\":\"6e2c3b41-1acd-479a-a1ba-7120c4115374\",\"next_chunk_id\":\"1b605a55-c01a-4bfc-9e5c-7f630de174a8\",\"quality_score\":100.0,\"should_use\":1},{\"chunk_id\":\"1b605a55-c01a-4bfc-9e5c-7f630de174a8\",\"file_id\":\"6d1dc034-2a37-4157-b297-449b5eb29b24\",\"chunk_index\":4,\"content\":\"Before a model can reason, it must be trained on massive high-quality data to learn patterns applicable to next token predictions. To demonstrate how data is ingested, we'll use a hybrid approach where the system performs a web crawl to extract real-time data, while referencing pre-trained vocabularies to ensure the model generates meaningful output. This process consists of the following steps:\\n\\n- Raw web crawl: Extracts raw text data from targeted websites.\\n- Heuristic filtering: Filters out low-quality content like non-natural language and isolated code fragments.\\n- Deduplication: Identifies and consolidates duplicate content across different sources.\\n- Tokenization: Maps the text data into tokens, implementing byte-level tokenization from scratch.\",\"content_type\":\"prose\",\"estimated_tokens\":143,\"section_header\":\"Data Curation &amp; Preprocessing\",\"parent_section\":null,\"top_header\":\"Data Curation &amp; Preprocessing\",\"prev_chunk_id\":\"e0fe3291-662f-4e13-b497-c60c6641f750\",\"next_chunk_id\":\"272def33-0774-4c01-b55c-3c76e2f60587\",\"quality_score\":100.0,\"should_use\":1},{\"chunk_id\":\"272def33-0774-4c01-b55c-3c76e2f60587\",\"file_id\":\"6d1dc034-2a37-4157-b297-449b5eb29b24\",\"chunk_index\":5,\"content\":\"To engineer data pipelines, we'll leverage web crawling. Web crawling can be performed either manually or systematically.\",\"content_type\":\"prose\",\"estimated_tokens\":21,\"section_header\":\"Data Pipeline Engineering\",\"parent_section\":null,\"top_header\":\"Data Pipeline Engineering\",\"prev_chunk_id\":\"1b605a55-c01a-4bfc-9e5c-7f630de174a8\",\"next_chunk_id\":\"cc69ad3c-af8e-462c-b5e7-2c6cbd5f0451\",\"quality_score\":80.0,\"should_use\":1},{\"chunk_id\":\"cc69ad3c-af8e-462c-b5e7-2c6cbd5f0451\",\"file_id\":\"6d1dc034-2a37-4157-b297-449b5eb29b24\",\"chunk_index\":6,\"content\":\"The most intuitive approach is a manual crawl , which involves accessing a website directly via its URL. In this mode, the crawler functions like a standard web browser:\\n\\n- Request: It pings a specific, live URL.\\n- Latency: It waits for the server to respond before proceeding.\\n- Single-threaded: It processes only one site at a time.\\n- Dynamic: Because it targets live sites, the data retrieved changes if the website is updated or goes offline.\",\"content_type\":\"prose\",\"estimated_tokens\":94,\"section_header\":\"Raw Web Crawls (Manual Crawl)\",\"parent_section\":null,\"top_header\":\"Raw Web Crawls (Manual Crawl)\",\"prev_chunk_id\":\"272def33-0774-4c01-b55c-3c76e2f60587\",\"next_chunk_id\":\"d8f97373-c8c5-4507-a3d5-2499d090650e\",\"quality_score\":100.0,\"should_use\":1},{\"chunk_id\":\"d8f97373-c8c5-4507-a3d5-2499d090650e\",\"file_id\":\"6d1dc034-2a37-4157-b297-449b5eb29b24\",\"chunk_index\":7,\"content\":\"Common Crawl , on the other hand, functions as a massive, historical archive like a snapshot of the entire internet, rather than browsing the live web. It is the standard of training for LLMs like GPT. Compared to manual crawling:\\n\\n- No live requests: The system downloads large data files (WARCs) from Common Crawl, which contain pre-scraped data from thousands of sites.\\n- High velocity: Data processing is limited only by the hardware's CPU/GPU speed, entirely bypassing the bottlenecks of internet latency and connection stability.\\n- Massive throughput: Ingest thousands of websites simultaneously by reading compressed files rather than scraping URLs one by one.\\n\\nTo perform the common crawl, the system streams content from the WARC file to generate a continuous response:\\n\\n<!-- image -->\",\"content_type\":\"prose\",\"estimated_tokens\":160,\"section_header\":\"Common Crawl\",\"parent_section\":null,\"top_header\":\"Common Crawl\",\"prev_chunk_id\":\"cc69ad3c-af8e-462c-b5e7-2c6cbd5f0451\",\"next_chunk_id\":\"ccbac0af-6701-4c10-8463-c9d12be22cd1\",\"quality_score\":95.0,\"should_use\":1},{\"chunk_id\":\"ccbac0af-6701-4c10-8463-c9d12be22cd1\",\"file_id\":\"6d1dc034-2a37-4157-b297-449b5eb29b24\",\"chunk_index\":8,\"content\":\"```\\nfor record in records: if record.rec_type == 'response'  : # decompress the payload raw_payload = record.content_stream().read() # convert bytes to string (UTF-8) raw_html = raw_payload.decode(  'utf-8' , errors =  'replace'  ) yield raw_html\\n```\",\"content_type\":\"code\",\"estimated_tokens\":68,\"section_header\":\"Common Crawl\",\"parent_section\":null,\"top_header\":\"Common Crawl\",\"prev_chunk_id\":\"d8f97373-c8c5-4507-a3d5-2499d090650e\",\"next_chunk_id\":\"10979112-e27d-4baa-ac2e-81e93b97bb13\",\"quality_score\":65.0,\"should_use\":1},{\"chunk_id\":\"10979112-e27d-4baa-ac2e-81e93b97bb13\",\"file_id\":\"6d1dc034-2a37-4157-b297-449b5eb29b24\",\"chunk_index\":9,\"content\":\"In the context of LLMs, heuristic filtering refers to the process of using rule-based curation of training data, removing low-quality, repetitive, or irrelevant content.\\n\\nBecause LLMs rely on massive datasets to master language, noisy data is captured by default. Training on such unfiltered data leads to several critical issues:\\n\\n- Hallucinations: Learns and reproduces incorrect patterns.\\n- Bias and toxicity: Adopts harmful language or societal prejudices found in the raw text.\\n- Computational waste: Low-value data costs expensive processing power.\\n\\nHeuristic filtering ensures that the model learns only from high-quality human language. Common techniques include:\\n\\n- Language distribution: Filters out pages with a low ratio of alphabetic characters (e.g., raw CSS code or random symbols).\\n- Keyword &amp; blocklist filtering: Removes documents that contain excessive toxic language or placeholders.\\n- Repetition checks: Eliminates bot-like content where phrases are repeated unnaturally.\\n- Length constraints: Discards snippets that are too short to provide context or excessively long data dumps.\\n- Quality scoring: Uses metrics like the gunning-fog index or perplexity scores to ensure the text is readable and grammatically coherent.\\n\\nIn this project, we'll simply remove irrelevant contents:\\n\\n- HTML tags.\\n- Citations.\\n- A line longer than twenty (20) characters.\\n- Codes containing over three special characters.\",\"content_type\":\"prose\",\"estimated_tokens\":277,\"section_header\":\"Heuristic Filtering\",\"parent_section\":null,\"top_header\":\"Heuristic Filtering\",\"prev_chunk_id\":\"ccbac0af-6701-4c10-8463-c9d12be22cd1\",\"next_chunk_id\":\"4cf86892-4ec0-4adf-9892-5aa7ccde0fc2\",\"quality_score\":90.0,\"should_use\":1}]"' data-total-rows='60'
